item.title: uPAR CAR T — an intravenous CAR T cell that never enters the brain reverses cognitive aging by resetting the bone marrow myeloid progenitors that feed it
item.description:
Posted 2026-09-28 on bioRxiv (10.64898/2026.09.27.754777 v1): "CAR T cell targeting of inflammatory myeloid progenitors in the bone marrow remodels border-associated macrophages and reverses cognitive aging." Corina Amor corresponding (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory / HHMI), with Christopher R. Vakoc. CC-BY. The fourth organ system for the lab's anti-uPAR senolytic CAR, after liver fibrosis (Nature 2020), age-related metabolic dysfunction (Nat Aging 2024) and intestinal regeneration.
THE STRAIGHTFORWARD HALF. uPAR rises with age on brain immune cells. scRNA-seq of FACS-sorted uPAR+ (8,941 cells) vs uPAR- (20,177 cells) from 18-month-old mouse brains, annotated with Allen Brain MapMyCells, shows the dominant uPAR+ population is border-associated macrophages (BAMs) - meninges, choroid plexus, perivascular space - not microglia, and specifically the inflammatory BAM subset. A single intrathecal dose of 1x10^6 m.uPAR-m.28z CAR T cells (retrovirally transduced, mouse CD28 costim) depletes that subset, calms the surviving BAMs transcriptionally, lowers brain proinflammatory cytokine/chemokine protein, and improves novel object recognition, Y-maze spontaneous alternation and Morris water maze at 2.5 months, sustained to 6 months. Intravenous dosing does not put CAR T cells in the brain; intrathecal does, and they persist 16 months. Prophylactic dosing at 2 months of age leaves animals cognitively intact at 18 months. In PS19 (human MAPT P301S) tauopathy mice, one intrathecal dose at 2.5-3 months attenuates cognitive impairment, reduces tau accumulation, and increases median survival 37.8%. Selectivity matters here: only the uPAR+ inflammatory subset is removed, sparing the broader BAM compartment, which is neuroprotective in AD.
THE EXPERIMENT THAT BECOMES THE THESIS. Intravenous CAR T should be the negative control, since it does not infiltrate brain. It is not - IV dosing also improves cognition, also depletes uPAR+ BAMs, also lowers brain cytokines. The tell is kinetics: intrathecal reads out at 2.5 months, intravenous at 6. IV CAR T cells accumulate in marrow with an effector phenotype and delete uPAR+ HSCs, MPP1/2/3, GMPs and monocytes, all of which expand with age; the surviving uPAR- progenitors are transcriptionally "rejuvenated" (reduced age-related inflammatory and myeloid-bias programs).
THE LOOP-CLOSING TRANSPLANT. 18-month-old CD45.2 mice treated IV with UT or uPAR CAR T; 6 weeks later 2x10^5 myeloid-biased HSPCs harvested and transplanted into aged CD45.1 recipients (busulfan 20 mg/kg/day x 3 preconditioning), against a young-donor arm. Engraftment is equal across arms AND total donor-derived CD45.2 myeloid cells reaching the recipient brain is equal - so this is not trafficking, it confirms marrow progenitors are a BAM source in aging. What differs is fate: fewer uPAR+ donor monocytes, fewer uPAR+ donor BAMs, and recognition/spatial memory improved to the level of young-progenitor recipients. Bulk RNA-seq of sorted uPAR+ vs uPAR- Lin- marrow cells shows the uPAR+ fraction is inflammatory, and macrophages differentiated from uPAR+ progenitors in vitro inherit that program and secrete more inflammatory protein - i.e. the inflammatory state is heritable through differentiation. Non-cell-autonomous kicker: CAR-T-treated donor progenitors also reduced myeloid bias in the recipients' endogenous marrow and uPAR on endogenous CD45.1 monocytes.
HUMAN DATA (EXPRESSION ONLY, AND THEY SAY SO). PLAUR is highest in CNS macrophages across the human brain atlas and marks an inflammatory subset; in human prefrontal cortex myeloid datasets, PLAUR rises in perivascular macrophages with aging and Alzheimer's; in human marrow scRNA-seq, PLAUR rises with age across HSCs, MPPs, GMPs and monocytes. They also note PLAUR/PLAU pathway variants have been associated with AD risk.
WHERE THE EPISODE PUSHES BACK. (a) Entirely syngeneic mouse, mouse CAR, mouse CD28 domain, and no lymphodepletion in any CAR arm - busulfan appears only in the transplant experiment. A therapy that works with zero preconditioning in a mouse says little about the cost in a person. (b) The target is not expendable tissue: uPAR has a homeostatic role in young HSC mobilization, and the proposal is durable deletion of a fraction of the hematopoietic progenitor pool by a persisting, self-amplifying cytotoxic cell. That bargain is easy in r/r myeloma and very hard in a cognitively normal 60-year-old - and the prophylactic-in-youth result, the most striking thing in the paper, is precisely the indication where risk-benefit is least defensible. (c) The authors themselves flag that skull-marrow-to-meninges channels mean the intrathecal arm may also be acting on progenitors rather than resident BAMs. (d) Non-cell-autonomous BAM interactions with microglia/astrocytes are unexplored (their stated limitation).
REGISTRY CONTEXT THE EPISODE ADDS. A ClinicalTrials.gov sweep returns 97 studies mentioning uPAR or PLAUR and not one is a CAR. Human uPAR clinical experience is imaging and radioligand only - gallium-68 NOTA-AE105 PET (NCT02681640, NCT03278275) and Monopar's MNPR-101-PCTA-177Lu (NCT06980519). The target has been dosed and imaged in people, which is more de-risking than most preclinical CAR targets get, but the receptor has never been in a patient. Amor is listed as inventor on ~10 patent applications covering senolytic CAR T.
THE TRANSFERABLE SPINE. Every hard CAR problem in this listener's world is framed as a question about the diseased tissue - antigen density, epitope position, tissue penetration. This paper argues the tissue can be downstream: if the pathogenic population is manufactured somewhere accessible and carries a surface marker there, you can treat an organ you never enter, from a vein, with one dose. The obvious next question is autoimmunity, where the field is arguing about how deeply an autoimmune CAR T must penetrate lymphoid tissue for a durable reset.
item.itunes:summary: Today's pick went up on bioRxiv yesterday from Corina Amor's lab at Cold Spring Harbor, with Chris Vakoc. It is a CAR T paper with no tumor in it anywhere, and I am covering it because it makes an argument about where to point a CAR that generalizes straight back into cancer and autoimmunity. Amor's lab built the senolytic CAR years ago - a receptor against uPAR, a surface marker of dysfunctional proinflammatory cells - and has since aimed it at liver fibrosis, age-related metabolic dysfunction, and intestinal regeneration. This paper is the brain. The straightforward half: aged mouse brains accumulate uPAR on immune cells, and when they sorted and sequenced roughly nine thousand uPAR-positive and twenty thousand uPAR-negative cells from eighteen-month-old brains, the dominant positive population was not microglia but border-associated macrophages - the macrophages of the meninges, choroid plexus and perivascular spaces - and specifically the inflamed subset of them. One intrathecal dose of a million uPAR CAR T cells depletes that subset, calms the survivors, lowers brain cytokines, and improves novel object recognition, Y-maze and Morris water maze at two and a half months, still holding at six. In the PS19 tauopathy model a single dose drops tau and increases median survival by thirty-eight percent. A prophylactic dose at two months of age leaves animals cognitively intact at eighteen months. The experiment that turns this into a different kind of paper is the one that starts as a control. Intravenous dosing does not put these cells in the brain - they show that in figure one - so it should be the negative control. It is not. IV also improves cognition, also depletes the inflamed border macrophages. The tell is kinetics: intrathecal reads out at two and a half months, intravenous at six. You are not treating the brain, you are treating something slower upstream. That something is the bone marrow, where aged mice expand an inflammatory, myeloid-biased progenitor compartment carrying surface uPAR. IV CAR T cells accumulate there, delete the uPAR-positive fraction across stem cells and every progenitor tier, and the survivors look transcriptionally younger. Then they close the loop: take myeloid progenitors out of a CAR-T-treated old mouse, transplant them into a different old mouse, and compare against progenitors from a young donor. Engraftment is equal and, crucially, the total number of donor myeloid cells reaching the recipient brain is equal - so this is not trafficking. What differs is what they become. Recipients of CAR-T-treated progenitors have fewer inflamed border macrophages and memory as good as recipients of young progenitors. Macrophages differentiated from uPAR-positive progenitors in a dish inherit the inflammatory program, so the state is heritable through differentiation. Where I would push. Everything is syngeneic mouse with a mouse CAR and a mouse CD28 domain, and there is no lymphodepletion in any CAR arm - busulfan appears only in the transplant experiment. uPAR is not expendable tissue; it has a homeostatic job in young stem cell mobilization, and the proposal is to durably delete part of an aging person's progenitor pool with a persisting, self-amplifying cytotoxic cell. That bargain is easy in relapsed refractory myeloma and very hard in a cognitively normal sixty-year-old, and the prophylactic result - the most beautiful thing in the paper - is exactly the indication where the risk-benefit is hardest to defend. The authors also concede that skull-marrow channels to the meninges mean the intrathecal arm may be hitting progenitors too. For calibration: the trial registry has ninety-seven studies mentioning uPAR and not one is a CAR. The human uPAR experience is a gallium-sixty-eight PET tracer and a lutetium-one-seventy-seven radioligand. The target has been dosed and imaged in people; the receptor has never been in a patient. The reason this belongs on your radar even though it is neuroscience is the targeting logic. Every hard CAR problem you work on is framed as a question about the diseased tissue. Sometimes the tissue is downstream - and if the pathogenic population is being manufactured somewhere accessible, you get to treat an organ you never enter, with one dose, from a vein.
